channel.description: Noticias globales de insurtech, actualizadas cada 6 horas.

item.title: EigenRisk Integrates GeoX Property Data
item.description: “Bringing GeoX’s property data into EigenRisk gives underwriters and reinsurers a much clearer, parcel-level view of what they’re actually insuring,” comments Jacob Grob, EVP of U.S. (Image source: GeoX website.) EigenRisk (Ann Arbor, Mich.) has integrated GeoX (New York) property intelligence into its EigenPrism catastrophe-risk management platform. GeoX’s property intelligence dataset is integrated directly into EigenPrism, where users can augment exposure data with building attributes and analytics for their books of business.

item.title: Hurricane Lowell Brings Heavy Rains as It Passes West of Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lowell passed west of Hawaii, where heavy rains may cause hundreds of millions of dollars of damage. Lowell, with top winds of 105 miles (169 kilometers) per hour, edged west of Kauai but is still dropping heavy rain, as well as sending pounding surf across the US state and island chain, the US National Hurricane Center said in an advisory. “Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Lowell will overspread the Hawaiian Islands through Wednesday,” Brad Reinhart, a senior hurricane specialist at the center, wrote in a forecast analysis.

item.title: After $240M Bitcoin Theft, Crypto Scammers’ Spending Spree Comes to an End
item.description: The scammers — a network of young men in their late teens or early 20s — celebrated the August 2024 heist by embarking on a wild spending spree. Cybersecurity researcher Allison Nixon, who has spent years tracking The Com, an underground subculture of young hackers united by the “insane amount of money” that crypto fraud can generate, advocates for more law enforcement resources to go after them. history, duping a stranger out of bitcoin worth over $240 million.

item.title: OpenAI Commits $1B to Cyberdefense Effort Amid AI Safety Scrutiny
item.description: OpenAI has faced increased scrutiny since its own AI agent breached systems at open-source platform Hugging Face during a July test and attempted to hide its actions. OpenAI said on Thursday it would commit $1 billion in subsidized access to its AI cybersecurity tools, training and technical support for organizations that protect critical services, as concerns grow over increasingly sophisticated AI-enabled cyberattacks. OpenAI on Thursday, alongside the cybersecurity initiative, also unveiled Astra, a new AI model it described as its most capable yet but said can at times attempt to evade human monitoring.

item.title: Detroit Sees First Tornado in Nearly 30 Years
item.description: Severe storms last week in Southeastern Michigan led to the first tornado touchdown in 30 years for Detroit, according to a report from the National Weather Service. This was the first confirmed tornado in the city of Detroit since the F2 that impacted the city on July 2, 1997. The line also spawned a brief EF-0 tornado in Lincoln Park and an EF-2 tornado on the east side of Detroit.

item.title: There’s a massive amount of capital looking to enter our industry: Superczynski, Aon
item.description: The insurance and reinsurance industry has an opportunity to harness the appetite of global investors to support growth and help find the capacity to make more risks insurable, because “there is a massive amount of capital that’s looking to enter our industry,” according to Kelly Superczynski, Head of Global Capital Advisory at Aon’s Reinsurance Solutions. There’s plenty of capacity in the market, it’s just a matter of how we get people coming forwards.” Moving on to discuss the potential to grow the insurance and reinsurance industry’s capital base meaningfully, Superczynski said she sees no lack in capital appetite, just that the risks need to be made more accessible to investors. If you look at it in the context of a $250 trillion alternative investment market, our insurance industry is dwarfed by the amount of capital that’s sitting out there in investable capital.

item.title: Peak Re plans to reignite third-party capital business, partner with investors: CUO Hough
item.description: Peak Reinsurance Company (Peak Re), a global reinsurer headquartered in Hong Kong, has plans to “reignite” its third-party capital management business in 2027, seeing itself as having a differentiated offering for investors and wanting to become more sophisticated in the space, Chief Underwriting Officer Philip Hough told Artemis. The company has ambitions and plans underway to become more active again in the third-party capital management space, seeing partnerships with investors as a key way to grow its expanding global reinsurance business. Speaking with us in an interview at the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Hough explained that Peak Re’s third-party capital management unit, Peak Capital, remains licensed in Bermuda and ready to go.

item.title: ILS market structurally healthy, but faces crucial test in cycle management: Steiger, Icosa
item.description: Following several years of strong returns and renewed inflows, the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market currently sits in a structurally healthy position, however this recent momentum must be balanced with disciplined cycle management, Florian Steiger, CEO and Founder of Icosa Investments told Artemis in an interview. Steiger described the current state of the ILS market as “structurally healthy” and increasingly mature, whilst noting that the space continues to normalise following a number of exceptionally attractive years. Speaking to Artemis just before the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) reinsurance industry event, Steiger reflected on the current state of the ILS market, and also shared what Icosa’s views are regarding the rise of AI across the ILS space.

item.title: Vantage appoints Yves Charbonneau as Chief Risk Officer
item.description: (Vantage), a specialty insurance and reinsurance business, has announced the appointment of Yves Charbonneau as Chief Risk Officer. Marc Grandisson, Executive Chairman of Vantage, said, “Yves’s track record, from building enterprise risk frameworks in Bermuda to leading capital and reserving discipline across multiple platforms, reflects the exact rigour we need at the centre of Vantage’s risk function as we continue our momentum under Howard Hughes Holdings.” Charbonneau commented, “Vantage has built a dynamic, highly differentiated platform across the North American and Bermuda re/insurance markets. in Bermuda, including Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, and Head of Actuarial Function for Arch Re Europe.

item.title: EigenRisk expands EigenPrism catastrophe risk management platform with GeoX integration
item.description: EigenRisk, a provider of catastrophe risk management technology, has entered into a new agreement with GeoX, an AI-powered property intelligence company, to expand the EigenPrism catastrophe risk management platform, allowing clients access to granular, AI-derived property attributes across over 186 million US commercial and residential properties. “By pairing EigenRisk’s platform with our imagery analytics across 186 million US properties, we’re making it easy for teams to evaluate portfolio risk in seconds without getting bogged down by manual checks.” Last month, EigenRisk integrated Weatherwatch , an Australian company specialising in storm and weather risk management services, into EigenPrism. EigenRisk continues to expand its data partnership ecosystem with over 40 data providers in its platform, combining catastrophe analytics, hazard intelligence, and property attributes to deliver a more comprehensive view of risk.

item.title: Ceded US health insurance premium sees 300%+ growth over the past decade: AM Best
item.description: Over the past decade, the volume of ceded US health insurance premium to the reinsurance market has grown more than 300%, to USD 203 billion in 2025 from USD 59 billion in 2016, a new AM Best report has revealed. Ceded premium growth has been in double digits in three of the past five years, including 2024 and 2025 when ceded premiums increased by 30% or more. health insurance segments have been under pressure, prompting insurers to seek additional reinsurance support to manage large claims exposure and improve capital efficiency while looking to reduce earnings volatility,” said Jennifer Asamoah, senior financial analyst, AM Best.

item.title: A $320 Million Hack Exposes the Cracks in Crypto’s Plumbing
item.description: The $320 million hack of the Bitcoin-linked Liquid Network is another dent to crypto’s reputation as the industry tries to convince banks and institutional investors that digital assets can become part of mainstream financial infrastructure. The Liquid Network hack this week is the latest in a spate of breaches targeting decentralized platforms this year, including on Kelp DAO and Drift Protocol that together accounted for $588 million in losses. In this instance the hackers returned 3,400 of the Bitcoin, keeping about $47 million worth, according to Alex Thorn, head of research at crypto firm Galaxy Digital Inc.

item.title: AI Could Pose ‘Existential’ Risk to Humanity, UN Rights Chief Warns
item.description: rights chief Volker Turk warned on Monday that artificial intelligence could pose a threat to humanity, and pledged to press AI firms to reduce risks that his office said included disruptions to services, communications and democratic systems. “I share the concerns of industry insiders that advanced AI could pose an existential risk to humanity,” Turk told the body in Geneva. “I am calling here, today, for an all-out effort to put cast-iron guarantees in place around the safety and security of AI, before it is too late.” Turk did not elaborate on the nature of the risks but a spokesperson for his office said failures involving powerful AI systems could disrupt critical infrastructure and democratic institutions.

item.title: People Moves: Obusek Hired by Examination Resources as a Senior Manager
item.description: A longtime North Carolina insurance regulator, the woman who initially flagged billionaire Greg Lindberg’s raiding of his insurance companies’ reserves, plans to join an examination firm as a senior manager. She will then become senior managing director of strategy and operations for Examination Resources, an Atlanta-based firm that provides examination services for regulators, Captive Insurance Times reported . Examination Resources works with the National Association of Insurance Commissioners on accreditation and consults with state regulator departments on financially troubled insurance companies and receiverships, the company and the Times explained.

item.title: Markel introduces new cyber coverage
item.description: Markel will launch this month a new standalone cyber insurance solution in the UK for SMEs. The coverage supports businesses with revenue up to £250 million and covers more than 3,400 trade categories. The new coverage will be available on the Acturis platform.

item.title: Collinson secures £350 million credit facility
item.description: Collinson has secured a £350 million revolving credit facility from a syndicate of five international banks, doubling the size of its previous financing arrangements. “Securing this significant facility demonstrates the confidence that leading international banks have in Collinson, our strategy and our ability to deliver sustainable growth. The London-based company plans to invest £500 million over the next five years to expand its airport lounge network and Priority Pass offering, grow its insurance portfolio, develop new products and technology, and enter new markets.

item.title: NEOS partners with Marloo
item.description: Australian life insurance distributor NEOS Life has partnered with adviser productivity platform Marloo to integrate insurance pricing into advisers’ existing workflows. Marloo users can now access indicative pricing and projections for NEOS Protection, Encompass Protection and Futura Protection without leaving the platform. By integrating our NEOS Platform pricing capabilities into Marloo’s platform, we’re giving advisers the ability to compare a range of quality retail advice products and provide advisers with a faster and more seamless way to explore insurance options within the tools they already use everyday.” – NEOS Managing Director John de Zwart.

item.title: Las aseguradoras aceleran el aumento de beneficios
item.description: El beneficio conjunto de las aseguradoras españolas -cuenta no técnica- alcanzó 3.878,83 millones de euros en el primer semestre de 2026, lo que supone un incremento del 7,8% respecto al mismo periodo del año anterior, según datos de Icea.

item.title: Un mundo de riesgos más globales, frecuentes y difíciles de modelar no debilita al reaseguro
item.description: Las presentaciones de Munich Re, Swiss Re y Hannover Re en el Rendez-Vous de Monte Carlo dibujan un negocio reasegurador que se enfrenta a una siniestralidad cada vez más difícil de acotar, pero encuentra men esa misma complejidad los argumentos para defender su papel -y su precio- de cara a las próximas renovaciones.

item.title: Sabseg apuesta fuerte por su vertical de Health & Benefits y ficha a Jesús Santos como director comercial
item.description: Sabseg quiere liderar en cada una de las líneas de negocio en las que opera y ahora lo vuelve a demostrar en la de salud corporativa y beneficios para empleados.

item.title: British Police Try to Track Down Theft of 70,000 Pints Worth of Guinness Stout
item.description: British police have a stout task ahead: recovering 70,000 pints worth of stolen Guinness. “We will settle for nothing less than the full recovery of all the items stolen.” Related: Pabst Blue Ribbon Offers $20K Reward for Missing Beer From Truck Heist The Guinness had been destined for pubs, but was snatched Monday night by two drivers who pulled up to an industrial park in Runcorn and hauled away the trailers containing about 800 barrels of stout. this is real and we are deadly serious.” Police valued the Pabst theft from a Southern California warehouse at $70,000 and the company offered a $20,000 reward for information leading to the recovery of the stolen suds.

item.title: BASF Sues Apple in US, Says iPhones Infringe Face Authentication Patents
item.description: BASF sued Apple on Thursday, accusing the iPhone maker of infringing the German chemical company’s patented face authentication technology in many iPhone and iPad models. The complaint said Apple did not employ BASF’s patented technology when it launched face authentication, known as Face ID, in 2017 with the iPhone X, but now uses it in a variety of iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, iPad Pro and other products. “Apple knew or should have known of the high probability that updating its iPhones and iPads to incorporate Face ID using material and skin detection” infringed seven trinamiX patents, causing “substantial damages and irreparable injury,” the complaint said.

item.title: Help Me Understand: How Insurers Build Trust
item.description: And more than half of insurance customers surveyed by JD Power over the course of the last three years have low levels of trust in their insurers. The data is clear: Overall customer satisfaction—and customer trust levels—rise when U.S. auto and home insurance customers have confidence that they understand their policies.

item.title: Cedar Trace ILS bolsters its leadership. Fergus Reynolds to become CEO, adds new hire
item.description: Cedar Trace ILS, the Bermuda-based specialist insurance-linked securities arm of Cedar Trace Capital Management Group and closely linked to Mereo Insurance, has announced a range of leadership promotions and a strategic hire, which includes Fergus Reynolds being promoted to CEO. The moves come as Cedar Trace ILS looks to strengthen its investment management and operational capabilities in the insurance-linked securities market and the company said they underscore its commitment to building a specialist investment platform focused on underwriting discipline, portfolio diversification and risk-adjusted returns First, Cedar Trace ILS has named Fergus Reynolds to be appointed as its Chief Executive Officer, subject to regulatory, immigration and board approval. Reynolds joined Cedar Trace ILS in 2025 , taking on the role of Head of ILS.

item.title: Mt. Logan keeps focus on alignment, capital efficiency as offering expands: CEO Modin
item.description: CEO John Modin explained to us in an interview that the focus remains on ensuring alignment and delivering capital efficiency. (MLCM), the Everest Group owned and operated third-party capital management platform, has been expanding and diversifying its offering. Speaking with Artemis around the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Modin said that the evolution of Everest’s third-party capital platform brings new opportunities and optionality to investors that are seeking reinsurance-linked returns.

item.title: Abundant reinsurance capital a “window” to diversify before conditions shift: Madea, CEO HCMA
item.description: Today’s abundant reinsurance and insurance-linked securities capital levels presents the sector with a window of opportunity to diversify its capital stack and secure longer-duration solutions, before the market inevitably shifts again, Jarad Madea, CEO of Howden Capital Markets & Advisory told us in an interview. Going on to explain that, “Today’s abundant capital is a window to secure long-duration solutions before conditions shift, including multi-year reinsurance capacity, catastrophe bonds, casualty sidecars, or Funds at Lloyd’s. Most companies pour resources into growth strategies and give too little attention to what happens when conditions turn.” Madea urges his clients to start with an honest audit of their capital base and sources, to identify how diversified it really is and where that can be improved upon.

item.title: Abundant capacity and volatility are helping the re/insurance market innovate: Aon’s Lyons
item.description: “But what I think makes us most excited about this renewal season is that that increase in capacity, in capital and increase in volatility is also really driving increases in innovation.” During the briefing, Lyons reviewed market conditions for each line of business and highlighted the corresponding innovations emerging within them. The executive, who serves as CEO of Bermuda and Global Head of Products, argued that unprecedented capacity across nearly every line of business is a key opening for cedents to reset and future-proof their programmes against market volatility. In property, reinsurers continue to generate strong double-digit return on equity (ROE), with pricing still holding above 30% over the index at the height of the stock market, Lyons notes.

item.title: Cyber reinsurance market to shift focus to strategic deployment: Ariel Re’s Carr
item.description: Ample capacity and sustained competitive pricing will characterise the cyber reinsurance market, but the core discussion is shifting from sheer volume to strategic deployment, Daniel Carr, Head of Cyber Underwriting at Ariel Re, stated in a recent interview with Reinsurance News. We expect the discussion to move beyond simply how much cyber reinsurance is available towards how cedents allocate that capacity across the loss distribution.” This reassessment is driving a shift in buyer behaviour ahead of the January 1, 2027, renewals, where Carr anticipates a “more deliberate approach” centred on structure, attachment, and event definition rather than a dramatic pricing shift. According to Carr, as the reinsurance industry meets at Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) 2026 in Monte Carlo, the question for the market is no longer how much capacity exists, but where along the loss distribution cedents choose to deploy it.

item.title: MS Re’s Bruniecki says retentions to hold as attachment points stay disciplined
item.description: Especially, as casualty is such a diverse universe where risks are big and very volatile, I do think risk and rating go more hand in hand.” Turning to terms and conditions, and specifically attachment points, Bruniecki argued that discipline throughout the risk chain is what has kept retentions intact since the market reset of 2022. People will have to get disciplined in their underwriting because we cannot support business which is below technically adequate levels.” Casualty, in Bruniecki’s assessment, remains a different story, with rate adequacy still an open question given how varied the class of business is. I do think for the most part retentions will stay in place.

item.title: Seattle Times, Newsday Sue OpenAI, Microsoft, Alleging Copyright Infringement
item.description: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers’ journalism without permission to train their AI systems. A spokesperson for Microsoft, based near Seattle in Washington state, said in an email: “While we’re surprised by the lawsuit, we appreciate the importance of local journalism and we’re always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute.” The Seattle Times and Newsday are seeking an order requiring the destruction of copies of their works as well as training datasets or AI models incorporating them. The lawsuit echoes a case filed by the New York Times in 2023, which accused OpenAI and Microsoft of using millions of newspaper articles without permission to train OpenAI’s popular chatbot.

item.title: Viewpoint: Reinsurance Market to Experience Further Softening, M&A on Ample Capacity
item.description: Challenging Renewals as Softening Continues; Terms Weaken Fitch expects highly competitive market conditions in most property and specialty lines to drive further market softening in 2027. A materially elevated loss experience would likely be required to change the softening market trend. The global reinsurance market maintains a very strong capital position that has benefitted from favorable earnings in recent years, with solid underwriting profits and resilient investment returns.

item.title: Canada Loses 41,700 Jobs as Employment Shrinks in Finance
item.description: Employment in Canada fell by 41,700 in August, reversing some of the labor market momentum seen in recent months as the manufacturing sector posted the only significant increase. The finance, insurance and real estate category lost almost 10,000 jobs. The jobless rate held steady at 6.4% while job losses were concentrated in Ontario and Quebec, Statistics Canada reported on Friday [Sept.

item.title: Ransomware Trends in 2026 for Cyber Insurers
item.description: The biggest ransomware trends in 2026 are the shift from file encryption toward data theft, stolen credentials, cloud and infrastructure compromise, AI-assisted activity and cyber insurance accumulation risk. The most important ransomware trends in 2026 involve attackers moving beyond file encryption and targeting the identities, data, infrastructure and shared systems that organizations depend on to operate and recover. For cyber insurers, these developments make the complete loss chain increasingly important when assessing ransomware insurance claims, underwriting exposure and portfolio accumulation.

item.title: Why Human Audits of AI Decisions Fail
item.description: Ask an organization how it governs an AI-assisted process and, sooner or later, someone will say that a human reviews the decisions. Eventually, the organization can point to a documented human-review process while the overwhelming majority of AI-assisted decisions pass through without meaningful scrutiny. As AI scales, insurers relying on sampling to audit AI decisions may be kidding themselves.

item.title: Europea Seguros launches ChatGPT plugin
item.description: Spain-based funeral insurance provider Europea Seguros has launched a ChatGPT app developed by Waniwani . The app allows users to ask questions about funeral insurance and receive quotes using a birth date and Spanish postal code. Quote results can display plan pricing, payment frequency, and coverage details.

item.title: Aviva launches hybrid fronting offering for MGAs
item.description: Aviva has launched a hybrid fronting offering for larger, established MGAs through its Global Corporate & Specialty business. As demand grows for partners that can support international, multi-class programmes, our hybrid model gives MGAs, brokers and reinsurers a single route into Aviva’s global reach, specialist underwriting expertise and financial strength. The offering combines fronting capacity with risk retention and is designed for multi-country, multi-line insurance programs generating at least £20 million in gross written premium.

item.title: Liberty Specialty Markets adds security advisory benefit
item.description: Liberty Specialty Markets is providing eligible political risk policyholders with access to a security consultation from Blackthorn Risk Group. This investment is a clear demonstration of our willingness to provide a differentiated, market-leading offering to our clients.” – William Limb, Head of Political Risk Solutions, Liberty Specialty Markets. Clients purchasing qualifying political risk coverage through Liberty’s London team can opt in to a free 60-minute virtual session with a senior Blackthorn adviser.

item.title: Price adequacy is essential as ILS expands into casualty, specialty, and cyber: Artex’s Faries
item.description: As the ILS market expands its reach across casualty, specialty, and cyber, maintaining price adequacy remains a critical boundary for market growth. I think we have to watch the price adequacy and the softening to make sure that we don’t dip below a threshold that will cause investors to think about whether to deploy their capital elsewhere, but I don’t think we’re there yet.” As the ILS space continues to tap into hybrid, casualty, and specialty structures, operational complexity is also rising sharply. But it’s always a supply, demand, and return equation.” Turning to casualty, Faries explained that she sees sustained momentum ahead, adding: “Overall, I think there is further opportunity in casualty so we expect that growth to continue into 2027.” On specialty lines, Faries pointed to key market mechanisms facilitating institutional capital deployment: “Regarding specialty, we are involved in London Bridge 2 in the UK, which is the vehicle that efficiently delivers capital supporting Lloyd’s Syndicates.

item.title: Swiss Re expects to remain a meaningful participant in alternative capital: Baertschi
item.description: Speaking today at Swiss Re’s briefing at RVS 2026 in Monte Carlo, Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer, of P&C Reinsurance, underscored the importance of the reinsurers third-party capital markets focused Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) division, and stated that Swiss Re expects to continue to be a “meaningful participant in that market.” During Swiss Re’s media briefing at RVS today, Baertschi stressed the overall importance of the reinsurance industry having a strong capital base. The rest we think of as alternative capital as well.” Baertschi continued: “Alternative capital is an important part of the capital stack, and the opportunities that insurance companies and buyers of this kind of protection have, and it also very importantly supports the traditional reinsurance capacity.” In light of this, we asked senior executives what the reinsurer’s plans were for growing its Alternative Capital Partners division into 2027. Earlier this year, Swiss Re launched a new Alternative Capital Solutions unit to encompass its activities in ILS and retrocessional hedging and execution.

item.title: Cat bonds and casualty sidecars buoyant, but investors still don’t like surprises: Josefs, S&P
item.description: At the S&P Global Ratings briefing in Monte Carlo at the RVS, Maren Josefs, Credit Analyst at the company explained that the big stories in insurance-linked securities has been catastrophe bonds and casualty sidecars this year, but she cautioned the market to remember that investors still don’t like surprises. The protection gap between economic and insured losses is still widening across the globe, and at the same time, we have these new risks coming from geopolitics, climate, and technology advances, especially AI.” Moving on Josefs highlighted the two biggest sources of growth, as catastrophe bonds and reinsurance sidecars. Josefs stated, “The two main stories have been the cat bond market and the sidecars, especially on the casualty side.

item.title: Moody’s warns uncertainty around emerging risks could constrain re/insurance growth
item.description: “Insurers may want to tap into growth in emerging markets or new areas of risk, but uncertainty is high, and too many insurers don’t have the tools to understand the risks and grow meaningfully into these new areas.” Speaking at their firm’s briefing in Monte Carlo today, Brandan Holmes, SVP at Moody’s Ratings, and Joe Melly, Head of Casualty and Financial Lines at Moody’s Insurance Solutions, warned that insurers are navigating an increasingly interconnected and uncertain emerging-risk landscape. In his opening remarks at the briefing, held at the 68th edition of the Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS), Holmes suggested that the centre of gravity on insurance emerging risks is shifting.

item.title: Compre completes retrospective structured ADC transaction with Lloyd’s syndicate
item.description: Compre Group Holdings Limited (Compre), the Bermuda-domiciled international specialty reinsurance group, has reached an agreement on a retrospective structured adverse development cover (ADC) transaction with a Lloyd’s syndicate. Rachel Bardon, Chief Underwriting Officer at Compre, said, “This transaction is a strong example of how we are continuing to evolve our retrospective proposition to meet clients’ changing capital and balance sheet needs. The transaction covers the syndicate’s 2023 and prior Years of Account on a whole-account basis, spanning a multi-line portfolio of property and casualty business and assumed reinsurance, with subject reserves of approximately £200 million.

item.title: Closing cyber protection gap a major business opportunity: Munich Re
item.description: Speaking during the firm’s briefing at the 2026 Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) in Monte Carlo, Stefan Golling, a Member of the Board of Management of Munich Re, suggested that the industry has not done enough to close the significant cyber protection gap, while also flagging the major business opportunity in doing so as Munich Re looks to maintain its position as a market leader in the growing sector. He went on, “Closing the cyber protection gap is a major business opportunity, but it’s also our responsibility as an industry if we want to live up to the picture of being the immune system for our customers. Golling observed that much of the growth in cyber has come over the past 24 to 36 months and, with rates having softened, said he believes the industry has not done enough to close the significant protection gap.

item.title: Experian launches credit card app on ChatGPT
item.description: Experian has launched a credit card shopping app on ChatGPT, allowing users to discover and compare offers from its partner network without leaving the conversation. Those who want personalized offers are redirected to Experian, where members can view cards matched to their credit profile, including eligible preapproved and No Ding Decline offers. The launch expands Experian’s use of conversational AI across loans, insurance and credit cards.

item.title: domusIQ launches UK real estate MGA
item.description: Commercial real estate analytics platform domusIQ has launched a global insurance business and begun underwriting through a new UK MGA. The MGA will target commercial real estate, residential and commercial property owners, and commercial combined risks. domusIQ MGA (UK), hosted on the Davies MGA Services platform, began underwriting on August 1.

item.title: Simply Business renews Premium Credit partnership
item.description: Simply Business and Premium Credit have renewed their insurance financing partnership under a six-year agreement. Premium Credit will continue to support Simply Business through its finance platform and API integration, allowing customers to finance their insurance premiums. Simply Business serves small businesses and landlords in the UK.
